mainTopic: Outsiders who grab disputed land, quick ways a חזקה is set up and the need to protest, and a Jew who got land from a גוי.
overview: This עמוד first finishes explaining why רב נחמן's case is not split like סומכוס's case: here only one of the two people can really be the owner. נהרדעי then rule that if an outsider grabs such land, the court leaves it with him, based on רבי חייא's ברייתא that 'a robber of the public is not called a robber.' רב אשי disagrees: the outsider is a real robber, and the ברייתא only means he has no way to return what he took. Next the גמרא goes back to the משנה's three-year חזקה. רבי אבא teaches that if the old owner himself carried fruit for the holder, the חזקה is immediate. רב זביד adds that the owner is believed if he says he only brought the man in for the produce, but only within three years. רב כהנא explains that an honest owner should have protested, and the גמרא proves this from the mortgages of סורא. Finally רב rules that a Jew who got land from a גוי needs a שטר, just like the גוי, and רבא's follow-up begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why this case is not split like סומכוס's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. In סומכוס's case each side has a real money stake, so they split. In רב נחמן's case only one side can be the true owner, so splitting does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: [There] this one has a money stake, and that one has a money stake. Here, if it belongs to this person, it does not belong to that one, and if it belongs to that one, it does not belong to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question from just before this text: why didn't רב נחמן split the disputed land, the way סומכוס splits doubtful money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סומכוס's case, such as the young of a cow that was sold, each side once owned the animal, so each has a real share in the doubt. In רב נחמן's case the land came from the ancestors of only one of them, so one side has no claim at all. Splitting would hand half to someone who surely has no right to it, so instead the rule is כל דאלים גבר.

keyTerms.meaning: A real money stake or connection to the item
Here, in the case we are discussing
If it is this person's, it is not that person's. Only one of them can be the owner.
Whoever is stronger wins. This is רב נחמן's ruling for the case.

steps.whatToRemember: Splitting (סומכוס) fits when both sides have a real stake. When only one side can be the true owner, the ruling is כל דאלים גבר instead.

phrases.english: [There] this one has a money stake,
phrases.notes: 'There' means סומכוס's case, like the young of a sold animal, which the גמרא brought up just before this.

phrases.english: and that one has a money stake;
here, if it belongs to this master, it does not belong to that master,
and if it belongs to that master, it does not belong to this master.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא, אִי דְּמָר – לָא דְּמָר, וְאִי דְּמָר – לָא דְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question (asked before this text) of why רב נחמן did not rule like סומכוס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a real stake on both sides versus a claim only one side can truly have.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought any doubtful property should be split, as סומכוס rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting fits only when both sides have a real money stake. Here only one does, so the rule is כל דאלים גבר.

steps.title: An outsider who grabs the disputed land keeps it
steps.stepSummary: נהרדעי rule that in a כל דאלים גבר case, if a stranger grabs the land, the court does not take it away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרדעא say: If someone from the marketplace came and took hold of it, we do not take it out of his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: נהרדעי add a new rule: if a stranger with no claim takes over the disputed land, the court leaves it with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither of the two people arguing can prove the land is his. So neither can show that the stranger took it from him. Their source comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city נהרדעא
Someone from the marketplace: a total outsider with no claim
Took hold of the land and started using it
We do not take it out of his hands

phrases.english: The scholars of נהרדעא say:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בָּא אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק, וְהֶחְזִיק בָּהּ –
phrases.english: If someone from the marketplace came and took hold of it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the disputed land from רב נחמן's case, where whoever is stronger wins.

phrases.english: we do not take it out of his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: אִם בָּא אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק, וְהֶחְזִיק בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the כל דאלים גבר case and asks what happens when a third person grabs the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An outsider who grabs land in a כל דאלים גבר dispute is not removed by the court.

steps.title: Support from רבי חייא: a robber of the public
steps.stepSummary: נהרדעי support their rule with רבי חייא's ברייתא: someone who robs 'the public', where the victim is unknown, is not called a robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: A robber of the public is not called a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source for נהרדעי's rule: a ברייתא taught by רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'robber of the public' is someone whose victim is not known, so no one can come forward and demand the item back. נהרדעי compare this to the outsider: since we don't know whose land it is, no one can force him out.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught a ברייתא
A robber of the public: one whose victim is unknown
He is not called a robber

phrases.english: As רבי חייא taught:

phrases.aramaic: גַּזְלָן שֶׁל רַבִּים לָאו שְׁמֵיהּ גַּזְלָן.
phrases.english: A robber of the public is not called a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for נהרדעי's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: נהרדעי's ruling that the outsider keeps the land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ברייתא: גזלן של רבים לאו שמיה גזלן.

steps.title: רב אשי: he is a robber, he just can't give it back
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the 'robber of the public' really is a robber. The words 'not called a robber' only mean he has no way to return what he took.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He really is called a robber. So what does 'he is not called a robber' mean? That the item cannot be returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains רבי חייא's ברייתא another way, which takes away נהרדעי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For נהרדעי, the ברייתא meant the robber is not treated as a robber at all. רב אשי says he is fully a robber; the ברייתא only means he has no one to give the item back to, so he cannot fix his wrong by returning it. So רב אשי disagrees with נהרדעי's ruling itself: the outsider is a robber, and the land is taken away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (used to keep the plain meaning)
And what does it mean?
Able to be returned to its owner

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say the robber is innocent. He says the opposite: the man is a full robber, and his problem is that he has no way to give the item back.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
He really is called a robber,
so what does 'he is not called a robber' mean?
That it cannot be returned.
phrases.notes: He doesn't know whom he robbed, so he has no one to give it back to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם שְׁמֵיהּ גַּזְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from step 3 differently, so it no longer supports נהרדעי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the way נהרדעי read the ברייתא they used as proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Not called a robber' does not mean he is innocent. It only means he cannot return the item.
steps.whatToRemember: נהרדעי: the outsider keeps the land, based on 'a robber of the public is not a robber'. רב אשי: he is a real robber; the ברייתא only means he cannot return what he took.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: three years from day to day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a חזקה takes three full years, as a lead-in to the next teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their חזקה is three years, from day to day, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its three-year rule. This sets up the comments that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that for land and similar property, a holder only gets a חזקה after three full years of use. The next steps will show cases where this works differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Their חזקה: proving ownership by using the property
From day to day: three complete years
Etc.: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: חׇזְקָתָן שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Their חזקה is three years, from day to day, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on land takes three full years.

steps.title: רבי אבא: an instant חזקה when the owner carried fruit himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא teaches that if the old owner himself carried a basket of fruit for the man holding the field, the חזקה is set up right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: If he himself lifted a basket of fruit for him, it is a חזקה immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives a case where no three years are needed: the old owner himself helped the new holder carry the field's fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally three years of use show that the holder must have bought the field. But when the old owner personally carries fruit for him, he is acting as if the field belongs to the holder. So that act alone sets up the חזקה right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifted up
He himself: the old owner
A basket of fruit
Immediately
Accepted proof of ownership through use

phrases.english: רבי אבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי דָּלֵי לֵיהּ אִיהוּ גּוּפֵיהּ צַנָּא דְפֵירֵי,
phrases.english: If he himself lifted a basket of fruit for him,
phrases.notes: 'He himself' is the old owner, and 'him' is the person now holding the field.

phrases.english: it is a חזקה immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: אִי דָּלֵי לֵיהּ אִיהוּ גּוּפֵיהּ צַנָּא דְפֵירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the משנה's three-year rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the old owner himself carries fruit for the holder, the חזקה is set up right away.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that three years is not magic. What matters is clear evidence that the old owner treats the land as the holder's.

steps.title: רב זביד: the owner is believed if he says 'I brought him in for the fruit'
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the old owner can still be believed if he claims he only brought the man onto the field to work it for the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: And if he claimed, 'I brought him down for the produce,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד adds a limit: the old owner can explain that he let the man in only to work the field and take produce, not as an owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the owner carried fruit for him, the owner may say the man was only a worker or sharecropper, someone who was always allowed to take the fruit. If so, carrying fruit does not show a sale, and the owner is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a claim in court
For the produce (only to eat or work the fruit)
I brought him down: I let him onto the field
Believed

phrases.english: רב זביד said:
And if he claimed and said:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the old owner, the one who carried the fruit in רבי אבא's case.

phrases.english: 'I brought him down for the produce,' he is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד, וְאִם טָעַן וְאָמַר: לְפֵירוֹת הוֹרַדְתִּיו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The old owner is believed if he says he brought the man in only for the produce.

steps.title: Only within three years
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד's rule that the owner is believed works only within three years. After three years, he is no longer believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies within three years, but after three years, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a time limit on רב זביד's rule: the owner's claim is believed only within the first three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before three years, the holder has no full חזקה, so the owner's explanation is accepted. Once three years have passed, the holder has the normal three-year חזקה from the משנה, and the owner's 'only for the produce' claim no longer helps.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only...
Within three years
After three years

steps.whatToRemember: The three-year חזקה usually needs three full years. רבי אבא: if the old owner carried fruit for the holder, the חזקה is immediate. רב זביד: the owner is still believed if he says 'only for the produce,' but only within three years.

phrases.english: And this applies within three years,
but after three years, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּתוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ, אֲבָל לְאַחַר שָׁלֹשׁ – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a time limit on רב זביד's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner's 'for the produce' claim is believed only within three years, not after.

steps.title: What could the owner have done to protect himself?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא: if the owner really did bring the man in only to eat the produce, how could he have stopped him from getting a חזקה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: If the owner really brought him onto the field only to eat the fruit, what was he supposed to do?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a fair question about the rule from Step 8. If the owner was telling the truth, how could he have protected himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said that after three years the owner is no longer believed when he says 'I only let him in for the produce.' But what if that really was the deal? רב אשי wants to know what an honest owner was supposed to do so that he would not lose his field.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought him down (onto the field)
Fruit, produce
What was he supposed to do?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
If he brought him down for the produce,
phrases.notes: This is the owner's claim from Step 7: 'I only let him onto the field to work it for the fruit.'

phrases.english: what was there for him to do?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: אִי לְפִירָא אַחֲתֵיהּ, מַאי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֶעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how fair the three-year limit from Step 8 is for an honest owner.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What an honest owner should do to keep from losing his field after three years.

steps.title: He should have protested
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the owner should have made a protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He should have protested.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the owner could have protected himself by protesting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner was not helpless. If he had protested, he could have made it known that the man was only there to eat the fruit. Because he stayed quiet for three years, he only has himself to blame.

keyTerms.meaning: He should have
To protest (from the word מְחָאָה)

phrases.english: He said to him: He should have protested.
phrases.notes: The one answering here is רב כהנא.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner should have protested during the three years. Since he did not, his loss is his own fault.

steps.title: Proof from the mortgages of סורא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that protesting is the solution. Otherwise, in a סורא-style mortgage, the lender could hide the document and claim he bought the land, and the חכמים would never set up an arrangement that leads to loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't say this, look at the mortgages of סורא. They say: 'When these years are over, this land goes back to the owner without money.' If the lender hid the mortgage document and said 'I bought it,' would he be believed? Would the חכמים set up something that leads people to a loss? Rather, the owner should have protested. Here too, he should have protested.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב כהנא's answer with a real-life case: the special kind of mortgage used in the city of סורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a סורא mortgage, the lender lives on the land and eats its fruit for a set number of years, so he can hold it for three years or more. If he could just hide the contract and say 'I bought it,' owners would lose their land, and the חכמים would not allow an arrangement like that. So the protection must be that the owner protests, and the same answer works for our case.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortgage, a field given as security for a loan
סורא, a city in בבל
Hides, keeps hidden
Purchased
A loss
For if you do not say so (opens a proof by showing the other option makes no sense)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'loss' here is the owner's loss. The danger is that the lender keeps the land forever by hiding the mortgage document.
steps.whatToRemember: An owner who lets someone hold his field must protest. If he stays silent, a חזקה can be made against him. This is true even for a field given as a mortgage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: when an owner's silence could cost him his field, the way to protect himself is to protest.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
these mortgages of Sura,
in which it is written:
"At the completion of these years
this land will go out without money";
phrases.notes: He means the land goes back to its owner without the owner paying anything. The years of fruit pay off the loan.

phrases.aramaic: אִי כָּבֵישׁ לֵיהּ לִשְׁטַר מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא גַּבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: if he hides the mortgage document with him,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender who is living on the land.

phrases.english: and says: It is purchased and in my hand,
would he really be believed?
Would the Sages set up
something that leads people to a loss?!
Rather, he should have protested;
here too, he should have protested.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, הָנֵי מַשְׁכְּנָתָא דְסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that רב כהנא's answer in Step 10 is correct.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that an owner protects himself from a חזקה by protesting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The mortgages of סורא. Unless protesting protects the owner, the חכמים' arrangement would lead to loss, and that cannot be.

steps.title: A Jew who got land from a גוי is treated like the גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a Jew whose claim comes from a גוי is like that גוי. He can only hold the land with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A Jew who comes through a גוי is like a גוי. Just as a גוי has no חזקה except with a document, so too a Jew who comes through a גוי has no חזקה except with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. רב gives a rule about a Jew who got his land from a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי cannot hold land through three years of use alone; he needs a שטר. רב says a Jew who got the land from that גוי steps into the גוי's place. So his three years of use do not help him either. Only a document does.

keyTerms.meaning: Who comes through a גוי (his claim to the land comes from a גוי)
A claim of ownership based on holding and using the land
A written document, a deed

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A Jew who comes on account of a gentile –
phrases.notes: He means a Jew who got the land from a גוי.

phrases.english: he is like a gentile;

phrases.aramaic: מָה גּוֹי – אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: just as a gentile has no presumption of ownership except with a document,
so too a Jew who comes on account of a gentile –
has no presumption of ownership except with a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: יִשְׂרָאֵל הַבָּא מֵחֲמַת גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the three-year חזקה rule from Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew whose claim comes from a גוי, like the גוי himself, can only hold the land with a שטר.

steps.title: רבא begins a follow-up case
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a follow-up: what happens if the Jew makes a certain claim? The rest of the case continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And if the Jew said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening line. רבא is setting up a follow-up to רב's rule, and his full statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is about to describe a claim the Jew might make that could change the outcome of רב's rule. For now, all we know is that the case depends on what the Jew says.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he said

phrases.english: Rava said: And if the Jew said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a follow-up case to רב's rule in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not finished here. רבא's ruling continues on the next עמוד.
